newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ASTON VILLA SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ASTON VILLA SQUAD.

text.p: Pen pictures of players expected to comprise the Aston Villa squad for Saturday's English premier league match against Arsenal:

Mark Bosnich, goalkeeper, Age 24. When Australian international Bosnich last visited north London he made headlines for all the wrong reasons -- giving Spurs fans the Nazi salute. Would prefer to make news this time for his goalkeeping which has been curtailed this season by illness and injury.
Michael Oakes, goalkeeper, 23. Reserve keeper who has impressed during Bosnich's absences.

Steve Staunton, defender, 27. Joined Villa for 1.1 million pounds ($1.8 million) from Liverpool in August 1991 after winning championship (1990) and F.A. Cup (1989) at Anfield. Versatile and consistent at left-back, central defence or midfield.

Ugo Ehiogu, defender, 24. London-born central defender who is tipped to become an England regular over next few seasons. Strong, hard-to-beat defender who played two league matches for West Brom before signing for Villa for 40,000 pounds in July 1991.

Alan Wright, defender, 25. Only 5ft 4 ins (1.62 metres) tall, but that has not stopped him becoming an excellent left-back. An occasional member of the Blackburn team that went on to win the title in 1995, he joined Villa in March 1995. Made his league debut for Blackpool as a 16-year-old.
Carl Tiler, defender, 26. Made his league debut as a 17-year-old for Barnsley in the 1987-88 season before spending five seasons at Nottingham Forest.
Riccardo Scimeca, defender-midfielder, 21. Of Italian parentage, made his debut for Villa at the start of last season. Versatile youngster who is establishing himself in the side.

Ian Taylor, midfielder, 28. Was Brian Little's first signing for Villa from Sheffield Wednesday in December 1994. Valued at 1.0 million pounds in a swap-deal that took Guy Whittingham to Sheffield Wednesday.

Andy Townsend, midfielder, 33. Celtic are reported to be interested in signing Townsend whose contract at Villa is up at the end of the season. Republic of Ireland international and club skipper, Townsend is often at the hub of Villa's build-ups. Previously with Southampton, Norwich and Chelsea.
Mark Draper, midfielder, 26. Played for Brian Little at Leicester then moved to join him again at Villa for 3.25 million pounds in July 1995. Former England Under-21 international.

Fernando Nelson, midfielder, 24. Joined Villa for 1.75 million from Sporting Lisbon in the summer and has settled well into English football, giving Villa a variety of options which has strengthened their overall game.

Savo Milosevic, striker, 23. The great enigma. Undoubted technical ability, good movement, possesses great pace and an eye for a goal, but unfortunately for him and Villa his shots often end up in Row Z. The Yugoslav seemed set to leave Villa for Perugia in November, the deal fell through and now he is back -- as enigmatic as ever.

Dwight Yorke, striker, 25. Born in Tobago and possesses outstanding ball skills. Scored 17 league goals last season -- has got 11 so far this. If he maintains his form all season, Villa stand a realistic shot at the title.
Tommy Johnson, striker, Joined Villa from Derby in January 1995. Clinical goalscorer who has been out of the side this season.
Julian Joachim, striker, 22. Another former Leicester player, Joachim re-joined manager Brian Little at Villa in February.
Sasa Curcic, midfielder, 24. Former team-mate of Milosevic's at Partizan Belgrade, Curcic moved to Villa Park for a club record fee of 4.0 million pounds from Bolton at the start of the season.
